headline: Medium prompt-injection and cascading-error risk from OpenBBTerminal’s MCP/API surfaces into taipy’s data-engineering workflows; no direct evidence of shared channels or writes.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: OpenBBTerminal exposes MCP servers and APIs, so its outputs can be consumed as structured input; taipy is a data-engineering tool that may ingest upstream outputs. No shared channel is documented, but the MCP surface plus taipy’s workflow role makes instruction-like content plausible. Uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF OpenBBTerminal output is routed into taipy task inputs or prompts without sanitization, injection becomes plausible.
IF a shared MCP or message channel is configured between the two agents, the risk increases.
mitigations: Disable any automatic prompt forwarding between agents.
Add a strict allowlist parser for OpenBBTerminal outputs.
Insert a human review step before taipy consumes OpenBBTerminal text.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all inter-agent messages.
requires-engineering: isolate the agents onto separate channels/workspaces.

B_data_leakage.rationale: OpenBBTerminal touches financial, licensed, and public data, while taipy’s profile shows no data classes or egress. There is no documented shared filesystem or upload path, so leakage is not established. The main concern is accidental transfer of sensitive financial data through manual or configured handoff, which is limited without a known bridge.
conditions: IF OpenBBTerminal outputs financial or licensed data into a shared handoff channel, leakage becomes possible.
IF taipy is configured to persist or forward received data to external systems, exposure increases.
mitigations: Keep sensitive OpenBBTerminal outputs out of shared folders.
Turn off any automatic export from OpenBBTerminal to taipy.
Use redacted sample data for integration tests.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent workspace isolation.
requires-engineering: add DLP checks on inter-agent transfers.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: OpenBBTerminal cannot write the filesystem or modify git state, and taipy’s profile exposes no write or git capabilities. With no overlapping mutable-resource writes documented, direct capability conflict is limited. The only plausible conflict is coordination around shared runtime resources, which is not evidenced here.
conditions: IF taipy is deployed with additional write or git permissions not shown here, conflicts may emerge.
IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable workspace through external orchestration, contention can occur.
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only where possible.
Avoid sharing a writable project directory.
Run them in separate processes or containers.
requires-engineering: add locking around any shared mutable resource.
requires-engineering: define explicit ownership for files and jobs.

D_cascading_error.rationale: OpenBBTerminal can produce financial-modeling outputs that taipy may consume in data-engineering workflows. If taipy treats those outputs as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream transformations or scheduling. No verification step is documented, so the interaction is plausible even though direct evidence is absent.
conditions: IF taipy consumes OpenBBTerminal outputs without validation, incorrect financial facts can propagate.
IF taipy triggers downstream jobs from those outputs, the blast radius expands to multiple work products.
mitigations: Add schema validation before taipy accepts OpenBBTerminal output.
Require a second source check for financial facts.
Log and review all cross-agent handoffs.
requires-engineering: implement confidence thresholds before downstream actions.
requires-engineering: separate generation from execution roles.

E_compliance.rationale: OpenBBTerminal explicitly touches financial and licensed data, while taipy’s profile does not show regulated data handling or residency constraints. There is no direct evidence of a residency or certification mismatch, so this is a limited compliance concern rather than a breach. The other agent is not cited for a specific regime because none is documented.
conditions: IF regulated financial data is routed through taipy in a jurisdiction with stricter retention rules, compliance gaps may appear.
IF OpenBBTerminal outputs are retained longer than policy allows, the mismatch becomes material.
mitigations: Minimize regulated data passed to taipy.
Set short retention on shared artifacts.
Review data-handling policies before integration.
requires-engineering: document residency and retention boundaries.
requires-engineering: add deletion/export workflows for shared data.
